reply_text:
I found one candidate for Shane Legg in 2015, and it's a weak one. It comes from the Edge.org answer to the 2015 Annual Question ("What do you think about machines that think?"), called "General Purpose Learning Machines." I read it on Edge's own site. Two things to check before you use it:

- **It may not be his alone.** The essay is written as "we," and one search snippet showed Demis Hassabis's name above Legg's on the page. So it may be a joint essay. The page I opened didn't show the top of the page, so I couldn't confirm this myself.
- **The time span is loose.** The only time-related wording is "a generation of talented researchers." I'm treating "a generation" as a length of time, but you could reasonably rule it out under rule 3. The page also gives no exact date, only that it's the 2015 Annual Question.

The same essay says human-level AI is not "just around the corner." That has no date, so I put it under undated.

Nothing else turned up from 2015. Legg was on a panel at the Future of Life Institute's Puerto Rico conference (January 2–5, 2015), but the event page I opened has none of his words. His well-known line "Human level AI will be passed in the mid-2020s" is dated to 2008 by some sources and 2016 by others, so it goes under other_years.

I used all 12 searches and 3 of the 6 page openings. The first search ran once; only my printing of its results failed, and I read the saved results rather than running it again.
